utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence that still applies. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Vasic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. I hope you still remember the warning I gave you yesterday, asking you to make a pause between questions and answers so that the interpreters can have the time to interpret it and so that your voice is not heard through my microphone. I would now like to go back briefly to the Borovo Selo events in May of 1991. When asked by my learned friend yesterday in examination-in-chief you said that most of police members who were killed in Borovo Selo were Croats. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The police of the Republic of Croatia, were its members in Borovo Selo before the events of multi-ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer your question with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you then know that most of the killed policemen were Croats?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I thought that they were, but I didn't claim that I knew for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday during examination-in-chief you also said that from one point in time until the 20th of November, 1991, you didn't have regular electricity supply in the hospital and that on those occasions you used generators to supply the electricity for vital equipment and lighting in the hospital. I'm interested to know whether these generators were used only for operating rooms in the hospital or perhaps for some other premises as well.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were used mostly for operating rooms, but also for the purposes of the atomic shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said for atomic shelter. Now, tell me, please, what type of equipment was supplied by electricity from these generators.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you gave us your position concerning the liberation of Vukovar. When asked by my learned friend, you said there was no need for anybody to liberate you, that you lived peacefully prior to that. We're now referring to the autumn of 1991 and I have to ask you something. Did you hear that prior to the beginning of the conflict in Vukovar there had been explosions, that some people had gone missing? Do you think that these people that had gone missing also had their families, their lives, their homes?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at one point they became victims of terror and somebody had to protect them from it. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned your colleagues Ivankovic and Manojlovic. Do you believe them to be responsible individuals, professionals?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend yesterday asked you whether you had ever seen any weaponry in the hospital. He even said that that -- he inquired about the anti-aircraft weaponry, and you responded that you had never seen something like that. What would you say if I told you that Dr. Ivankovic and Manojlovic said in their statements that there was firing which originated from the hospital aimed at the JNA airplanes?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a great deal of respect for these colleagues of mine as people and as surgeons. Now I would like to reiterate that I have no such information that there was any firing from the hospital, that any fire was open from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to clarify another issue which was brought up yesterday in one of the questions of my learned friend. You said that at one point in time you moved into the basement of the hospital, and that from then on you slept there. I'm interested now to know whether this basement is in the old or new building of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the old part of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the personnel who worked in the kitchen slept, are you aware of that, in which building of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also in the old section of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to turn to the last day you spent in the hospital, the 20th of November. Yesterday you said that there was a meeting held that morning in the hospital, and upon leaving that meeting, as you were walking to your room to collect your belongings, you noticed the hospital was empty. I suppose when you said that you did not have in mind the patients who were lying in their beds, who remained in the hospital later, on the 20th and 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I think I said that the hospital was almost empty. And yes, you are right, there were patients in beds, not all of them but some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that on the 18th of November you were formally informed that there would be an evacuation of the hospital and that it would be conducted under the supervision of the International Red Cross. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this day you also probably were aware that there would be an evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I would agree with you as regards that question. Until the last moment, we believed we would stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because yesterday you told us --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps it would be better if we moved into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, that concludes your cross-examination, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, my colleagues will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the public understand now what has happened. Yes. Thank you. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Borovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I am Borivoje Borovic, representing Miroslav Radic. The first question: What was the name of the chief of your ward?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I have a mental block. Perhaps you can assist me. You must know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness answers the question, I ask that we move into private session because of these names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army -- therefore, the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army has existed in Vukovar since what time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten, 20 years at least, but I wouldn't be able to be more specific. At any rate for a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the barracks?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we were children, our schools went to tour the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the events in Vukovar, did you pass by the barracks?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need for me to go in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we can conclude that from May until late November you never passed by the barracks. Would you please give an audible answer?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just waiting for the interpretation to conclude; that's why I was hesitant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you spoke about the planes of the JNA that were shot down. You said that you were not in Vukovar on that day but that you read about it in the media. What did you read about it? Who had shot down those planes?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the information that was given was that two planes were downed. As for who precisely had done it, I wouldn't be able to say with certainty; therefore, I would rather not answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist us with this. Later on during your stay in the hospital, did you perhaps hear who might have downed those two JNA planes?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not inquire about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were there ethnic streets in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that we can accept that fact if you know nothing about that, namely the fact that the Serb houses and Croat houses were intermixed throughout the town in various streets?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us something about this. How was the JNA able to know which houses it fired on? Or can you tell us this: Was it only the Croat houses that were damaged or did the Serb houses suffer damage as well?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire city was targeted and hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you wish us to conclude that the JNA fired upon both Croats and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the people lived throughout the city, if they were mixed, intermixed, and if there were no ethical borders, then, yes, one would come up with the conclusion that you gave us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then can you explain further the goals of the JNA that you referred to yesterday. If the JNA attacked Serbs as well as Croats, then what goals did they have?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the case, you would have to address your question to a JNA representative because it involves military objectives and goals, and this is not something that I'm competent to discuss. This falls within the military domain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Madam, but this is something that you spoke of yesterday and you gave us your conclusions about these military issues despite the fact that you are just a doctor. Do you have an answer to this question or do you not wish to answer it?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a specific answer to give you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The atomic shelter in the hospital, I remember what you said yesterday concerning that. Therefore, my question will be very specific. When did they start preparing this atomic shelter for use? During what months were the preparations begun?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was in September but I may not be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will try to put to you the words of the witnesses who testified here before you. The first two witnesses who were employed in the hospital stated -- we don't need to go into private session. This is something you're aware of and we will not be mentioning any names. They stated that on the 2nd of May, 1991, the atomic shelter was prepared. The director of the hospital was quite determined when she spoke of that. What's your comment?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If she claims something like that, then it must be true. I have no such knowledge. I didn't go to that part of the hospital. I can only tell you when we approximately started using it. As for the preparations, I know nothing about that. Those who were in charge of the preparations would be better placed to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you then allow for the possibility that the -- that the shelter was indeed prepared, that the preparations were started back then in May of 1991? Do you allow that that is possible?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the atomic shelter at Borovo Komerc was prepared, another atomic shelter that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility of this to have occurred in May 1991?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If those responsible said so, there is no reason for me to state otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we can see from your written documents as well as from the statements you gave the investigators in the Dokmanovic case as well as your testimony yesterday, there are numerous references to the ZNG. My question is: The National Guards' Corps, in your opinion was it a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find that question difficult to answer, frankly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The way the Defence sees things, that too is a very good answer. Did you know what a paramilitary soldier known as Zenga, member of the ZNG, looked like? Did you ever see one of those wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A military uniform, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what the uniform looked like, what the weapons looked like and what the insignia were like? I don't mean the rank, I mean the sign, a badge, or insignia that were the distinguishing feature of that particular paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't describe the weapons because I don't understand about weapons. I can tell you that it was a camouflage uniform, but I couldn't describe it more specifically than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you don't seem positive about this, please allow me to help you. The insignia worn by that paramilitary formation, does it have the letter U on it?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never ever seen such insignia on any of the informs that I saw at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is not meant to taunt you; it's meant in a very serious manner. Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber who are the Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that I came across back in school. It's something from the dark and distant past and is something to do with World War II when there were a number of paramilitary formations around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please share with us part of your recollection at least in relation to this paramilitary formation known as the Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I think back to what we studied at school, those were nationalistic units. They had a nationalistic charge, as it were, or bias. I think that would probably best describe them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which nationalistic environment or set did this emblem that you've just described to us belong to?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There is information, some of it has been discussed between this Trial Chamber, to suggest that comparisons were drawn at the time between the ZNG and the Ustasha. I'm not sure if you're aware of that, the implication being that the ZNG were seen as a continuation of the Ustasha, another paramilitary formation from World War II. Were you in fact aware of the fact that comparisons were being drawn by the two units?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You belong to another time and I do not wish to take you back to this distant and mirky past. My next question: Do you who Franjo Tudjman is?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first Croatian president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be kind enough to explain, what does this mean, the first Croatian president? Did Croatia not have a president before him?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A president of the Croatian state, once it had declared independence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to that, had you been living in a Croatian state and did it have its own president?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in the Republic of Croatia, which was part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a president, this Republic of Croatia that was a state?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It always had a representative who was the representative of that particular republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this representative's name, the one before Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that for you the history of Croatia begins with November 1991?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope the Prosecutor and the Trial Chamber don't mind. So when does the Croatian history begin for you? Since you're an intellectual, I believe I'm entitled to ask you this question.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatia had a history before these events and after. Croatia was not created at this point in time; Croatia goes back a long time. But your question is in relation to very specific things before and after. As to when Croatia first came into existence, well, Croatia had existed as a republic, if that's what you want me to answer. You can take that to be an answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That I find a very satisfactory answer in fact. My next question: Do you know that President Franjo Tudjman in July 1991 visited Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in August 1991 the then-Croatian Prime Minister Franjo Greguric also visited Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to remind you of a fact, and I'll do it by asking a question. On the 8th of August, the secretariat for Vukovar's People's Defence adopted a decision to issue permits allowing persons to leave town, and that it was only those in possession of such permits, that is after the 8th of August, 1991, were allowed to leave town.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear about this, but I can't be positive about this. Personally I never needed that sort of permit, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that you heard about these permits and who told you?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that such permits existed, but not from anyone in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, is that a convenient time? We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that life in Vukovar was good before this happened, that you had good relations with your neighbours who belonged to other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer the following question. Were you personally in favour of Croatia's secession from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Trial Chamber permits, I would like to decline to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That, too, can be construed as a political position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go closed session for the next question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed or private? Private will do, I suspect? Closed means when we pull all the shutters down and -- yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Until when did the surgical ward have electricity?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think until the end of October or maybe November. I'm not absolutely sure. I'm talking about a continuous supply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said to The Hague investigators on page 2, paragraph 5, I can show it to you, and the Prosecutor can check that there was electricity until the very end in the surgical ward. What is correct?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you take into consideration that they had generators, those are two different issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who cut off the electricity, if anyone, and where this could have been done, because we are not from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say somebody cut off the electricity. I'm saying the installations and powerlines were damaged, and that's why there was no longer a continuous supply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that this Vukovar in the period you are describing, if we recall your reply about water yesterday, that nobody physically cut off the water and electricity supply to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that nobody did that physically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. In view of your profession, which I will not repeat in open session, how did you come by information concerning the number of patients that the hospital in its entirety admitted as you were only in one specific ward of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said something about these facts in the last session, and I noted this down. As you put forward this information, I'm asking you as someone working in a particular ward - and of course I won't say which one - how and on what basis could you know how many patients turned up at the hospital on a daily basis, the hospital as a whole?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to that is very simple. As a doctor working under those conditions, you're not there just physically. During the day, if necessary, you visit other wards, including the surgical ward. But when such things happen, you're physically present in those places where the largest influx of patients is so as to be nearby, should your assistants be needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you able to inspect the protocol on the admission of patients for the entire hospital or not?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now another question that does not concern my client directly but I feel could be significant for the Chamber. Do you know the difference as to why those who died in hospital were wrapped in white sheets and those who died elsewhere were not? Why was this done?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this. I'm not aware of this and I see no logical reason for it if it was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the wounded and for members of the paramilitary units known as the Zengas and the policemen who were brought to the hospital, the people who brought them in, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in the directed mission. When a patient came to me, at that point in time he had absolutely no weapons with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct when a patient arrives in your ward. But you said I think just a while ago that you did participate in the admission of new patients. And at that point, which is now of importance for the Defence, can you tell us whether at that point it was armed men who brought these people there; and if they were armed, what happened to the weapons.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I did know was that there was a rule in the hospital that weapons were not allowed to be brought into the hospital. They had to be either left outside the hospital or they were confiscated as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As for outside the hospital, all right. But as for confiscating weapons, do you know who confiscated the weapons, where they were stored, who was in charge of the confiscation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who had to do this, I know such persons existed, but whether they confiscated weapons, where, and where they stored them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you know, Madam, that there were persons who did that, tell us, were they members of police or the ZNG? Or perhaps it was a third party who also was a member of the medical staff.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my director would be better placed to answer that question. I don't have an accurate answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your director did answer that question. I can even remind you that the hospital had internal security which consisted of policemen. She gave us that reply, and you asked that I convey to you. Therefore, my next question is: Was internal security of the hospital -- did it comprise Vukovar policemen?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what she said, then that's how it was. But I, myself, didn't see any uniformed policemen there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that policemen, regardless of whether they were in uniform or not, provided internal security to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that there was security in the hospital to the effect that no one was allowed to bring in weapons into the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear that there was also external security?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can assist you. When you were leaving the hospital, or rather, I suppose that occasionally you left the hospital and then came back, as you stated. In those cases, as you were leaving in the yard or in the area surrounding the hospital, did you see any members of police or ZNG?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean beyond the hospital compound?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But in the vicinity of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people armed? You say that you saw them.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were in the premises that you described to us and thus unable to see what was happening outside, do you believe it possible that they were also able to fire from these weapons? Do you believe it possible?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say that, yes, it was possible. Now, whether they did it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber and Defence what type of weapons these were.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When on the 19th of November under the auspices of the Red Cross and Zeljka Zgonjanin, as you explained to us civilians left, my very specific question is as follows: Did the doctors remain in the hospital, members of their families, ZNG, and police members?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I would add civilians as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These civilians, were they members -- family members of the medical personnel as well as family members of ZNG and police members?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians were also the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you. Please don't take me wrong. My question is quite specific. Were civilians family members of the medical staff employed in the hospital and members, family members, of the ZNG and police members at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that civilians were family members. That is how I comprehend the term civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that when the JNA members entered the hospital their attitude was quite proper and decent. Can you elaborate on this. What did you mean by this? You described it quite fairly, so could you give us some more details.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I saw the groups of soldiers coming in, I was able to see that their attitude was quite decent. They didn't abuse anyone, either verbally or physically. It was a proper, decent attitude of anyone entering anybody else's premise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you stated that there was one Red Cross marking. You showed us where it was in the yard between the two hospital buildings.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, if you're able to give us a logical answer, is: Why was this marking not placed on the roof of the hospital, as is typical pursuant to all regulations that you're aware of, regulations concerning how to mark a hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at the time it was physically impossible, because who could be forced or who could be given a task to go and climb the roof of the hospital when there was constant shooting and firing that would put their life in danger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is: Did you ever stand in a spot where the marking was during those three months? Did you stand there or around that spot?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass through that yard between the old and the new building during those three months?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one was to look across the Danube from that spot, would one be able to see the Danube and also what was on the other side of the Danube, on the other bank?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that position, one cannot see the Danube.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that if there was somebody on the Serbian side of the Danube and shooting from there, then that person would be unable to see the Red Cross marking that you just described to us?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that question really falls under the military questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where the infectious diseases ward was?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know how to describe it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall I assist you? The Defence is only interested in how many storeys, if any, that ward had and whether it had a slated roof.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a one-storey building. It just had the ground floor and a slanted roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that that building also could not be seen from the other side of the Danube, as I just described it to you?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, you're trying to get me into the territory of military questions. No, one could not see it from the distance of 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know then how distant the hospital and that spot is from the other side of the Danube that I just described to you, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this marking removed? And if so, when?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information about the place of residence of the then-director of the hospital called Vesna Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was a neighbourhood in the vicinity of the hospital. It was a private house, I think. Somewhere nearby but I don't know the exact location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Vesna Bosanac slept during that time, whether she slept in the hospital every night just as you did?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think she slept there every night. I think she went home, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you elaborate on that. You had close contacts with her. She was the director. Once director leaves, somebody has to substitute for them. Therefore, please tell us, did she go home? What did you hear? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this; I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know how she went home? What did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean how?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she walk?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was able to, but I don't know the exact location of the house, therefore I cannot confirm with certainty that she in fact did go on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is: Vesna Bosanac, did she drive around Vukovar in a car in those days and months?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those days, yes -- in those months, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that cars were able to travel through the streets and that movement was unhindered? Perhaps you have an explanation for the fact that she was driving around the streets of Vukovar while the war was going on.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't misunderstand my reply. I have no intention to provoke you, but let me just say that people drove around Sarajevo when there was shooting as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. People did the same in Belgrade, but I don't think that we need to go into those topics today, either Belgrade or Sarajevo. My next question is: Do you know whether your director ever left Vukovar and went to some other towns during September, October, and November?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the main headquarters of the ZNG staff was located? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that it existed?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is simply how information is conveyed. When there are a lot of people in one place, people mention it. But I couldn't tell you who specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the employees of the Vukovar Hospital members of the ZNG staff?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When I put this question to you, I was referring to the defence staff of the city of Vukovar. That was clear to you?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what Durandal bombs are?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of that type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Durandal bombs, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what cluster bombs are?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I read, these are bombs that disperse into small fragments. That's what I know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen such a bomb?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fortunately not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever have any patients injured by phosphorous bombs?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that that wasn't typical for the kind of work performed in your hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude that possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude a possibility that somebody treated patients for such injuries. However, that was not within my area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that you never came across such a case in your career?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw different cases of wounding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But can we agree that you never saw this type of wounds in your professional career?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, I saw different cases of wounds. I saw burns. Now, as to how these burns were caused, by what type of weaponry, I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive information that somebody's burns were caused precisely by this type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there came a time when several persons were admitted to the surgical ward with this type of injuries. I personally didn't treat these patients.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the hospital director stated that there was just one person who came with symptoms consisted with -- consistent with injuries caused by that bomb, how can I reconcile your answer saying that there were several such cases? Because Dr. Bosanac was quite adamant. She said there was just one single patient with that type of injury?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that we should believe Dr. Bosanac's words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, I haven't checked the transcript. My recollection is that Dr. Bosanac described one case, but I don't recall her saying that that was the only case. I don't think she was asked that. She certainly described one case. You're -- I suspect you may have taken the further step of saying, Well, as she described only one, there was only one. But I don't think that was specifically her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid that she seemed quite decided in answer to my question. We can check that during the break. I am nearly certain that I was the one who asked her the question and that she seemed quite decided in her answer, but I will no longer be pursuing this topic for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated on the 17th hostilities ceased and that citizens started streaming in from many different parts of town. Did you spend that whole day in the hospital, the 17th of November?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The answer is?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend the whole of the 18th in the hospital from dawn till dusk, as it were?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there absolute peace at this time? And was the hospital a safe place for all these citizens to go to and feel safe? Or rather, in order to avoid the use of the word "safe," let me try and say that they could feel secure.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what they came there for, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that nothing was happening any longer in terms of shelling or bombing and that's why they felt secure?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was certainly no shelling on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that in your words we can be entirely certain that at 8.00 in the morning, at 10.00 in the morning, at 3.00 in the afternoon the hospital was not being shelled or bombed? I'm talking about the 18th of November. We can be absolutely positive about that, can't we?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness the following document on the screen, it's Exhibit 34. Your Honours, I see we're having a bit of difficulty with the technology, and the witness has virtually answered all of these questions. And I will withdraw this evidence. The Defence were merely trying to make a point by using this document, but I think the point's already been made, and there is no reason to use the document now. I would like to ask my next question, if the Court permits me, to skip over the line of questioning that I had proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a JNA soldier named Sasa. I believe you mentioned him yesterday in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you were the one who mentioned him, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you asked about the JNA soldier named Sasa Jolic yesterday?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were the one who mentioned him yesterday, not me, because I wasn't the one asking the questions yesterday. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I was referring to your colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was he exactly inside the hospital? Was he in the atomic shelter, where most of the patients were, in one of the corridors or in one of the rooms that were not inside the atomic shelter?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, he was not in the atomic shelter. He was in other rooms, just like all the other patients were once we had run out of room inside the atomic shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about the ward where the mentally ill were treated?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what my information indicates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the hospital have a ward of that description?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those patients the last to be evacuated into the atomic shelter, the last of all your patients? Is my information on this correct?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say because I was not working in that ward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the paramilitary ZNG members were most often brought into your hospital from? Because you did say yourself after all that you were there several times when they were brought in. Did you ever ask where they had been brought in from?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since most patients were of Croat ethnicity, I think we agree on this, during the war and the war operations, where were Serbs being treated?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea where you got the information that most were Croats, because as far as I know both Serbs and Croats came. No distinction was made based on people's ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Defence is using evidence presented in this trial, and witnesses who came before you testified about precisely this information, that after May 1991 Serb patients stopped coming to the Vukovar Hospital. However, since you seem to be challenging that, would you please then be so kind as to give us the exact percentages of Croat patients and Serb patients respectively, or are you not able to say that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to give you that sort of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this soldier, Sasa Jolic, brought into the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in November, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if this was a JNA soldier who had been captured or how did he get to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question accurately either, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, why does this seem to be a soldier that you all know about? Would that perhaps imply that there were so few of them or just those three who you treated?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not just because there were so few of them. They were, after all, JNA members, and yet they were received by the hospital and admitted just like all the other wounded who came in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sasa Jolic as a JNA soldier, was he perhaps being held hostage in the hospital because of the observers who were supposed to arrive in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The atomic shelter at Borovo Komerc, who was it used by?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never in that shelter, but according to my information it was used to accommodate wounded persons, but it was used by people over in Borovo and the surrounding neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court, please, despite the efforts that you were making, I fail to understand why people were arriving in the hospital on the 17th and the 18th.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what's so questionable about that. Many parts of town had been destroyed. People were spontaneously moving towards a place which they felt was still safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would that place be seen as safe, if, as you said, the hospital had been shelled continuously? Why did these people then believe it would be a safe place to go?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's something that people tend to feel in situations like these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you perhaps agree with me if I told you that this was in fact a movement which was thoroughly organised by the hospital on the one hand and members of the ZNG on the other?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could accept the position that it was well organised as a medical institution. But if you're implying anything else, no, I can't accept anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try to remind ourselves of the testimony you gave yesterday. I will ask you a couple of questions about that. You said you came to the hospital which you believed to be a safe place because your house had suffered a direct hit, was hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could -- could you then explain the circumstance that your parents decided to stay in that very house if it had indeed been bombed and shelled and destroyed, if what you told us yesterday is true?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's be perfectly accurate about this. I said the house had been hit once. I believe this is accurate. You can go back to my statement to verify that bit of information. I do have to say that my parents did indeed stay behind, and they stayed until the very end. This is a peculiar thing about old people in general. They're stubborn and they refuse to accept anything you tell them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Does that mean that the house was never shelled again after that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only later that it was really shelled and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't get me wrong, I hate to be asking questions about personal things. But how could they stay there?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting you wrong, but believe me I don't understand this myself. And if I may be allowed to, to just add something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Are we in private session at the moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think this requires private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. If I agree, does that mean that it's been redacted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be redacted when I sign a piece of paper, and at the break the technicians delete that section from the tape before the outside broadcast goes out. There's always a half-hour delay on the outside broadcasts, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You are really, really helping us along in this trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question, something I've broached already. You said your husband stayed behind in Vinkovci to fight because he was unable to reach Vukovar. This being the month of September, if I tell you that Dr. Vesna Bosanac testified she still could drive to Vinkovci on a number of occasions in November, is that something that you can comment on as true, or would you say it was true that your husband was unable to reach Vukovar, or was it perhaps the case that his military assignment was in Vinkovci?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll be quite specific in my answer to this question. My husband did not join in September. If you know about the fact that he went to Germany, then you should know that it was -- wasn't possible for him to be there in September. It was on the in late October or November, but not earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thank you for this piece of information. This is the most recent version, I must say, because in your statement to the investigators it says that he left for Germany on the 23rd of September, but it states nothing about when he came back. And this is, after all, your husband. If indeed he came back in November, when was it, if you were not in touch and if he never came to see you. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still stand by my previous testimony that he never visited me. But it was only after we had left, and I was not in touch with him at the time. I can only tell you that I found out about this based on what I learned from him later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's your husband. You've answered all these questions that were intriguing us about your life. When did he then join the ZNG, this paramilitary formation? So it must have been either October or November? This is your husband I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to get a perfectly accurate answer, perhaps you should go to him and ask him, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As, unfortunately, I don't have that opportunity I thought it might be a good idea to take advantage of you being here testifying. I thought I would have been better off perhaps talking to you rather than your husband. Thank you. Your statement was shown to you by my colleague from the OTP and my colleague Vasic. They were asking you questions about this statement. You stated as follows, if I may be allowed to refresh your memory. This is page 3. The OTP can follow. Paragraph 4, it says: "My estimate was that there were at least 1.000 people at the hospital" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I apologise for cutting in. It's just that I'm not aware that the OTP actually did show the witness her statement here during her testimony at all. Mr. Vasic may have done; I'm not sure about that. So perhaps if my learned friend could be a little bit more precise on those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Borovic, there was an attempt to do it and it wasn't successful. The Chamber was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not wish to oppose the Chamber, nor will I do so in the future, but I have to oppose my learned friend. I said as she was being taken through the statement provided to the investigators; I never said it was actually shown. But she was being taken by hand, as it were, through the statement, metaphorically speaking. However, if that's necessary, I can avoid being that specific and go back to the text in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you state to the investigators that many of the soldiers fighting in other parts of town were withdrawing to the hospital as each of the neighbourhoods fell? Is this something you stated?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I placed an objection on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Did you state that or did you not?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I had heard about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now my next question. You did not add anything to this passage, but to the next part when you said that you later heard that they changed clothes, took off their uniforms, put aside their weapons, put on bandages and plaster casts, but you did not correct the part that I have just read out to you. That's why I'm asking you, do you still abide by this. You said that you heard later that they changed clothes and so on?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will, if I may, say the same about this part. If I was inside physically, I could only hear this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would be a new addendum to the statement you gave the investigators in 1995 and the other day because you had nothing to add to this part then. You're only changing this part of the statement now, during this cross-examination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say I was changing it, only that I was adding to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While the meeting was going on in the plaster room, which you described, you said you saw your patients being taken away without an escort. The question is: The patients, your patients, who had the injuries that you registered, did they need a special medical escort?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under those conditions, my position is that they did need medical attendants, that they had to be escorted by medical staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even the policemen, whose name I won't mention, who had problems with his ears?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my medical supervision of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before I put my next question, I ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I have very few questions left, which is why I think I can finish in five minutes, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll sit on, Mr. Borovic. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June were you in the hospital in 1991?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time were sandbags placed around the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary in June, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this need arise, to put sandbags around the hospital, in what month?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did this? Was it you, medical staff -- I apologise to Their Honours. Was this done by doctors or other people?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not usual for doctors to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was it who put sandbags around the hospital for the protection of the hospital of course? Was it policemen, soldiers, or other people in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was the technical staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I say to you that I read a book by Dr. Njavro, have you done the same? It's a book about Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean did I do the same?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read Dr. Njavro's book? He worked in the hospital in Vukovar, and the book is about the events in the Vukovar Hospital in 1991?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't read the whole book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't read the whole book?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't read the whole book, or you haven't read the book at all?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read the book at all, just the title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you mean when you said "I didn't read the whole"?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw just the title and the introduction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If, as Defence counsel, I tell you that in this book Dr. Njavro, who dealt exhaustively with information about the Vukovar Hospital, stated that 80 patients died during those three months out of 2.000 treated, can you tell us that he provided erroneous information or was the information correct?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because this is not in accordance with what we heard, but I cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on the information provided to the public by Dr. Njavro, that on that occasion 600 members of the ZNG and policemen were killed in Vukovar and 6 to 8.000 members of the JNA, according to the information he collected. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I promised the Court, and you answered just as the Defence wished, I would like to thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. We'll have the second break now and resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- oh, Mr. Agha, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. The next witness has actually been waiting since morning, and I believe my learned friend may take some time in cross-examination. So I'm wondering if it's possible that he may be released for today, especially as I understand it takes ten or so minutes to disband protective measures, which the next witness does in fact not have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're encouraging us to waste time again, Mr. Agha. Yes, the next witness will not be required before tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- oh, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. But I did look through the transcript, as I promised, as regards the question about the 28th of October in connection with a question I put to Dr. Vesna Bosanac. Page 24, could -- pages 20 to 21. The answer was that only one person was killed by a phosphorous bomb -- was injured by a phosphorous bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. I'm sorry, but I had not correctly remembered. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day, Madam. My name is Novak Lukic, attorney-at-law, and I will put questions to you on behalf of the Defence team for Mr. Sljivancanin. My colleagues, who put questions before me, have already exhausted many of the topics. So I will try to contribute to the expeditiousness of these proceedings, but I may go back to some topics that have already been dealt with by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To begin with, I would like to briefly show the witness the photograph from exhibit 0053-1257, page 6 very briefly. It will appear on the screen. It will be a photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, do you recognise something in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the hospital buildings, if I'm right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, to the best of your recollection when did the new building begin functioning? I'm in the pre-war period.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was some ten or 15 years before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The then-building of the new hospital, that's what it was often referred to, the new and the old hospital, in 1991 was this building fully operational and fully equipped?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the building of the new part of the hospital? As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- I have learned that the top floor was not fully operational in 1991. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the attic or to the second floor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only read in some witness statements that the top floor of the building was waiting for a license to operate, but whether it was the second floor or whether it was the attic part, I don't know. But was there any part of the building that was at the top and that was not functional?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this may refer to the attic which still had to be put in order, but I don't know if we are referring to the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, it seems that in 1991 in terms of its size, did this building look as it appears on this photograph or not?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The size of the hospital was the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We will not be needing this photograph any longer. When giving testimony before this Court, you said that the Yugoslav People's Army was the aggressor's army. And according to you, there was no reason for them to attack, and there was no reason for you to defend yourself from anything or anyone because prior to that you led a normal life in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's how I understood it. In your opinion, after the change of authorities in Croatia, did all of the citizens of Vukovar lead a normal life?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information indicating otherwise. If I may clarify. In the street where I grew up and where I lived, a street that had residents of mixed origin, there were absolutely no changes in our way of life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not concerned at the time by stories that explosive was planted in certain facilities and that the people were disappearing?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a person, one certainly feels uncomfortable upon hearing that, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not concerned by stories that people were leaving their jobs?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say concerned. The better term perhaps would be surprised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you perhaps concerned or surprised by roadblocks which were manned by armed ZNG members, and one had to pass through those roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I pointed out, there were none in my part of the town, in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I linked that to the instance where you were leaving Vukovar, as you described to us and as you said to Mr. Vasic. When you had to pass through the roadblock when leaving Vukovar, you, as a citizen, were you concerned upon seeing something like that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One definitely feels uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is something that prompted me to proceed with the following line of questioning. It has to do with the uniforms. Do you remember whether the people manning the roadblocks had any uniforms; and if so, which type?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that there were both civilians there and people wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you lived in the street whose residents were of mixed ethnic origin. I assume you socialised with your neighbours at the time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your Serb neighbours tell you whether they trusted these roadblocks upon coming across them? Did they tell you anything about those roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep reiterating that there were no roadblocks in that part of the town. Naturally, we talked, we communicated, amongst us. But in that part of the town, we had no such unpleasant experiences, nothing that would give rise to these unpleasant feelings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you are trying to evade giving me an answer. In general terms, were Serb neighbours concerned about roadblocks existing throughout Vukovar and outside of Vukovar? And to play up what my colleague asked you, did you hear of your neighbours -- from your neighbours that they were concerned about these permits that one needed in order to leave town?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I hear that from my neighbours? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear stories that entire families started leaving Vukovar in the course of the summer, regardless of their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this give you an unpleasant feeling or did you still continue to believe that everything was normal?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was an uncomfortable feeling as such, it existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you will agree that, after all, the life in Vukovar in the last few months, or rather, in the spring and summer of 1991 was not quite normal?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say during the spring. It applied more to the summer-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to follow up to what you stated yesterday, you said that in your view after the incident in Borovo Selo, the conflict didn't escalate until August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something to that effect. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that yesterday when answering my colleague Vasic's question you said that you didn't know that the barracks in Vukovar was blocked and cut off. And then when answering the questions of Mr. Borovic, you said you had no reason to venture into that part of the town. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those early months, June, July, and even beginning of August, did you hear -- did you see the JNA soldiers walking about town, frequenting cafes, going there with their girlfriends? Do you remember seeing something like that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing them in the post office when I went there. I can't be very specific, but it was sometime in June or July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them in the post office in early August? Am I going into too many details? I'm asking you this because I want to refresh your memory and remind you of the fact that in the summer-time the barracks had already been cut off, placed under siege, and soldiers were unable to leave the barracks.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I said that I believed it to be in June or July. I didn't specify more closely the exact period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear perhaps during July or August the stories that the soldiers were freely able to leave town and go home, just as you were able to go and take your children out of town?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know about anybody asking that. I have no such personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that at the time you as well as all other citizens of Yugoslavia closely followed the reports on television and in the press. I'm now referring to the summer months of 1991.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say I was mistaken if I said that at the time the media reported that it was the policy of the Croatian leadership to place the barracks under siege and to hold the JNA personnel hostages? Did you hear such stories?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither confirm nor deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly go into private session, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when you gave evidence in examination-in-chief, we heard you say that according to what you knew corpses in the last days had been taken to the harbour -- harbour office. Now, tell us this, please: Did this pertain to those who died in the hospital or those who died elsewhere and were transported to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the procedure was in the hospital when a body of a dead person would be brought to the hospital? Were any records kept? Were any official records compiled where, you know, certain information would be entered about the post mortem, any details about the dead person, and so on?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, prior to all these events the regular procedure, if somebody died, was to perform an autopsy and to establish the cause of death. However, under these circumstances I think it was not done, although I have to say that I'm not fully certain about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who would be able to give us such information. Do you think Dr. Njavro knows more about this?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question on this issue. In your view, how far this harbour office is from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, 500 metres roughly. But don't consider this to be absolutely accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll leave this, then, for some other witnesses. I have another question of this nature. Previous witnesses gave us their assessment of distance, but we never put the following question to any of the previous witnesses. How far is the bridge over the Vuka River from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
