utterances.text: If my estimate is accurate, and I can't say that I'm an expert in estimating, then perhaps a kilometre or around -- thereabout. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll turn to another topic. Can we agree that there were no new patients in the hospital after the 18th? I think you stated that in your previous statements.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct. Now -- at least based on the information that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday also that, in your view, about 1.000 civilians came to the hospital. You even believed that everybody who remained in Vukovar came to the hospital. Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, did they also come there to await the evacuation that was expected?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one could interpret it in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see these civilians arriving in the hospital? Did you go through the areas where they were assembled?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of your occupation, and I'm not going to specify it, did you approval what was happening, namely that civilians were coming to the hospital and mixing with the patients?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of that specific situation, I thought that was logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your testimony, I understood that on the 19th of November, the situation in the hospital was quite chaotic. Everybody felt uncertainty about the upcoming evacuation. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said that this chaotic situation would not have existed had there been only those in the hospital who were supposed to be there, namely medical staff, the wounded, patients, and so on?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question calls for a very broad answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to provide a brief answer, and if the Prosecution wants to go further into this they will give you an opportunity to elaborate. My question is: Was the chaotic situation in the hospital a result of the fact that there were many people there who were not supposed to be there on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was not the only reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were other reasons?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, we didn't know what was going on. Therefore, all of us were distressed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were expecting the arrival of the International Red Cross based on the information you received about the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we were expecting at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those last days, your patients from your ward, did they stay together with all the other patients in some common area or were they staying separately in a separate area?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in different places throughout the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So everybody was mixed. They -- the patients were not classified and placed in various wards?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this distance, would you be able to tell us what was the influx in your ward in the last ten days of your stay in Vukovar? Let's say from the 5th or 10th of November, what was the daily number of newly admitted patients?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As -- at that point in time, we did not have strictly separated wards any longer. My answer would be four or five or six persons. The patients were not physically divided into separate wards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that anybody was discharged at the time from the hospital, from the ward? Were there people who no longer required any hospitalisation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, I think that there were one or two people who required minor interventions. I don't have information about their discharge. It's just that I didn't see them anymore. Now, I don't know whether they were actually officially discharged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you should know that, given that they are under your professional supervision?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't discharge them, but that doesn't mean that some of my other colleagues didn't discharge them from their wards, from their care.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If another colleague of yours discharged them, I assume they were supposed to inform you, since they were also under your care?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they had no such duty to inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go briefly into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received information that there should be evacuation and you described this to us, how did you - and I don't mean just you personally but everybody else under your care - prepare for the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the medical point of view, one had to revisit all aspects of the treatment. One had to put new bandages, give new instructions, tell them what it meant, how they should act. I gave them medication that they should have on them so that I wouldn't have to think about that any longer. Anyway, one had to go from one patient to the next, give them all the necessary information, and also re-examine them from the medical point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I was interested in. Was the appropriate medical documentation prepared for each patient, the documentation that should have accompanied these patients? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that patients were supposed to be classified based on whether they were able to move, whether they could sit, or just lie in beds?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is really a typical procedure, so I don't consider it remarkable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to classify patients based on those who were able to move and those who had to be transported in beds?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether in your group or in your ward you had any patients unable to move?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there injuries specific to your particular area of expertise, specialisation?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only mine but also surgical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when asked by the Prosecution, or perhaps by Mr. Vasic, you mentioned temperature charts. Can you tell us what this is and whether this is the document that reflects the medical history of the patient. I have to say that I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a temperature chart, a document, which is placed on the patient's bed. It contains first name, last name, type of illness, as well as therapy and the way therapy is administered, patient's temperature is recorded on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this document updated daily?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it should be, if you have the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My understanding is that therapy is reflected in the chart, too, daily therapy, and the patient's temperature.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the room where you spent the last few days? Were you able to clearly hear explosions and shells falling and exploding from there?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you stated in answer to a question by my learned friend, Mr. Borovic, that there was no shooting on the 18th or from the 18th on. Do you perhaps remember this, I want to know about the 18th and particularly about the 19th, did you hear individual shots or explosions being fired?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe sporadic or individual, but no artillery firing, if I'm not mistaken. But, please, one thing you have to keep in mind is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's not a trick question, if that's what you mean. I'm asking you about individual shots. Please tell me, who is Zeljka Zgonjanin? I believe you answered this one. Do you know what specifically she did at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name and surname. I know she was there, but I can't tell you what specifically she did or what specifically her tasks were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the name Sadika Bilus, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of your doctors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ward? What was her field?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was an internist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know her husband Davor?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear if he was ever at the hospital throughout those months? Is this something you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard that Director Bosanac asked you personally to go back to the hospital because the hospital needed you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from your colleagues, from your Serb colleagues who were leaving the hospital at the time, that she had asked them the same thing?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never talked to them about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago I asked you about preparations for evacuation, and you said -- or rather, you said that yesterday, that the medical staff had the task of monitoring the wounded during evacuation. You said so yesterday, and you confirm that now, don't you?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this something that you considered a rule for any evacuation or was this information that you were given as in, this is how it should happen?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered that to be a rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the medical staff escorting the wounded who were evacuated on the 18th of October, medical staff from the hospital? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to my information, there was several nurses accompanying them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever return?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We heard this from other witnesses. Are you familiar with such a concept as working group for evacuation? Did you hear that a group was organised in the hospital, people who were supposed to help with moving things and moving the wounded along?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 20th, on the morning of the 20th, the help workers of the hospital were supposed to be wearing white coats?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at all that there were help workers at the hospital who were volunteering?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The late husband of Binazija Kolesar, Mihajl, whom you knew stated to the OTP in a statement that he gave while he was still alive that Dr. Bosanac gave orders for help workers to put on white coats on that day. What is your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's his statement, that's what he stated, but it's not something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the 20th of November. You said that on the morning of the 20th a gentleman came to see you, as you said quite literally, and he was accompanied by Ms. Kolesar. However, in a previous statement you were more specific about the position of that particular gentleman. Based on your conversation, or perhaps on a gesture that this person made, or the way the person behaved, was there anything that led you to conclude what this person's position or occupation was?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember our conversation correctly, it's very difficult to repeat the whole conversation verbatim, it has been a long time after all, but I don't think I'll be wrong if I say that he addressed me as "colleague."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is literally what you said the last time around when you testified here, and that's why I wanted you to be more specific now. So your impression based on how he addressed you was that this gentleman was a doctor, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But sometimes when addressing other people ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you now about the meeting in the plaster room. Who told you to go to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurse Binazija at the very moment when we were having that conversation and she was just outside my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in your estimate the meeting took between half an hour and 45 minutes. You also said that you were standing near the door and you described how you left the room and went into the corridor outside. Do you remember if at the time you arrived the meeting had already begun or did you have to wait for the meeting to begin once you had arrived?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the meeting was just beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Mr. Sljivancanin was there when you entered the room?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time elapsed between the time Mrs. Binazija told you to go and -- or rather, did you go right away to the meeting or did you go a while later? I know it's been a long time, but can you please try to remember that.

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to be perfectly specific about the -- about time, whether it's 15 or 20 minutes. I really can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is quite sufficient for my purposes. It's a sufficient degree of precision for my purposes. Do you remember whether at the meeting there was another person there with Mr. Sljivancanin, somebody who was not part of your hospital team, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was another gentleman standing next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not the same man you had seen previously while you were with Mrs. Binazija, was it?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look him in the face, and I find it very hard to say whether it was or not. This is something that I don't remember at all. I have no recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you remember whether this man ever spoke to you during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to refresh your memory then. I will tell you what Mrs. Binazija Kolesar said in her testimony before this Tribunal. She said when she came to the meeting this man was the first to speak and Mr. Sljivancanin only spoke after him. Does that perhaps refresh your recollection? Was she at the meeting at the same time as you to begin with?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't listening all the time at that meeting. I said that clearly in my statement, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am trying to keep that in mind. I'm just trying to refresh your memory, but you can't rule out the possibility that this man also spoke at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't rule that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mrs. Bosanac at the meeting at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Dr. Njavro?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember or you don't remember seeing him?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that I did not see him, but it was quite crowded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name driver Zdenko Ragac mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that conversation, did you or any of your colleagues tell Mr. Sljivancanin what you had been doing up to that point? We'll not go into that again. I'm interested in those two bits of information that you gave to the Tribunal. Did you mention that to Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, as for myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of your colleagues perhaps mention that to Mr. Sljivancanin during that conversation? Did you perhaps hear that?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you share with your colleagues what you had been doing up to that point?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that you met Dr. Ivankovic. You described to us what you heard, what Mr. Sljivancanin said when he said that you would be allowed to stay at the hospital, that you could choose to go to Croatia or to Serbia. Yesterday when you testified in chief you told us why you remained in Vukovar. But why did you not remain in Vukovar at this point in time when you were directly offered to stay on and work at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that occurred to me after everything that had happened was to be reunited with my family. So that was the first thing that I wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the moment when you saw patients being led away down the corridor. You even emerged in the corridor at that time. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion were only patients leaving the hospital? What about the rest of the medical staff? And were there any civilians in the hospital at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. I really didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described that at one point in time you saw patients being led away past the emergency ward down that exit, down that corridor. Were these only patients or were civilians coming out at the same time?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only noticed patients.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When, roughly speaking, did you emerge in the courtyard outside the emergency ward in order to await evacuation on those buses?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it might have been around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you standing there, roughly speaking, before you boarded the buses?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think between one and two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps at this point see any of the international staff, European monitors, International Red Cross, somebody carrying a camera out there in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: P-O21 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything like that from the spot where I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have about five minutes left. I'm not sure what my learned friend from the OTP intends as far as re-examination is concerned. If he has no re-examination, maybe we could finish the witness now so that she doesn't have to stay for another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. Lukic, another case is listed to continue; that's why we must clear this courtroom at this time. So I must ask you to finish tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can no longer promise that it will only be five minutes in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm well aware. I was counsel for 34 years; I know how overnight refreshes one. We will adjourn now and we will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of November, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
